notes: INTENT: routes declared as CALLS rather than as files. Before audit fix C an Express app enumerated ZERO routes, LAW 2 was still satisfied because 0 === 0, and the coverage table printed a confident 'routes: 0' over an HTTP surface nobody had looked at — a silent blind spot, which is worse than a missed finding because it reads as completeness. All three handlers here are unauthenticated, and each must appear as its OWN subject: one file legitimately declares many routes, so the method and path are part of the subject or two rows would collide. Confidence is `needs-review` and not higher on purpose — the absence of an auth token in a handler is not proof, since the check could live in a helper this pass does not follow, and LAW 1 forbids turning a token's presence or absence into a verdict. Only the POST is asked to validate a body: the DELETE replies with res.json() and never reads one, and demanding validation there is the noise-on-correct-code failure that gets a report ignored. The fixed variant applies auth and a rate limit as app-level middleware before any route is registered — the recommended Express pattern, and the direct analogue of Next's middleware.ts — validates the POST body with zod, and scopes every query by the caller's id, so it must be completely silent.
